task.title: Give a phone held sideways a usable board
task.description:
Found in review of PR #217 (2026-11-22). The phone layout applies below 560 CSS px of width. A phone turned sideways is about 844 wide and 390 tall, so it gets the desktop layout: all columns side by side, the header and filters taking about 190 of the 390 px of height, cards draggable, and controls measuring 15 to 32 px (copy-ID 15, the remove buttons 24, close 32).

A rule based on a short viewport height on a touch screen, as well as width, would cover it. Decide whether sideways shows the one-column layout or a compact multi-column one.

Also from the same review: a task created from the bare /tasks/new address (no column chosen) is saved to its default status, and the board then returns to the column it was showing, so the new task is not visible and nothing says where it went.

## Done when
- At 844x390 and 932x430 with touch, the board, a task page and the new-task form are usable: no control under 44 px, dragging does not compete with scrolling, and the cards have most of the height.
- After creating a task, the person can see it or is told which column it is in.
